title: Popcorn Ceiling Removal Cost in 2026
description: Popcorn ceiling removal cost in 2026 by square foot, with asbestos testing warnings, DIY vs pro prices, and refinish costs.

cover.alt: Illustration of a room with a window on a painting blueprint background with a measuring tape

keywords: popcorn ceiling removal per square foot
takeaways: Pro removal runs $1 to $6 per square foot in 2026, and refinishing the bare ceiling is part of that top end.
Test for asbestos before you scrape any ceiling in a home built before the 1980s, and stop if the test is positive.
A 300 sq ft ceiling at a typical $4 per square foot, scraped and refinished, budgets to about $1,200.
body:
Popcorn ceiling removal cost in 2026 runs $1 to $6 per square foot with a pro, so most single rooms land between $300 and $1,500 finished. Angi's 2026 data puts removal at $1 to $6 per square foot, and HomeGuide puts plain scraping at $1 to $2 per square foot, rising to $2 to $6 once the ceiling is refinished smooth. The wide range is not a trick. Scraping is the cheap part, and skim coating, sanding, and painting are where the hours go. If your home was built before the 1980s, read the asbestos section before you touch anything.

## Popcorn ceiling removal cost per square foot

Quotes come in three layers, and you need to know which layers a bid includes. A scrape-only price leaves you with a rough, patched ceiling that still needs work. A scrape and refinish price leaves it smooth and ready for paint. A full price adds primer and ceiling paint on top.

| Job scope | Cost per sq ft | What you get |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Scrape only, no asbestos | $1 to $2 | Texture off, ceiling bare and uneven |
| Scrape, skim coat, and sand | $2 to $4 | Smooth ceiling, ready for primer |
| Scrape, refinish, prime, and paint | $4 to $6 | Finished ceiling, done |
| Removal with asbestos present | $5 to $20 | Licensed abatement, containment, and disposal |

Angi's 2026 figures put asbestos removal at $5 to $20 per square foot, plus $75 to $200 per hour in added labor for the specialist crew. That one test result can turn a $1,200 room into a $3,000 room, which is why testing comes first in every plan below. Ceiling size drives the rest. Angi lists a 500 sq ft ceiling at $500 to $2,500 and a 1,000 sq ft ceiling at $1,000 to $5,000, before any asbestos work.

Get each quote in writing with the scope spelled out line by line. One bid at $2 per square foot for scraping and another at $5 for a painted finish are not competing bids. They are two different jobs.

## Worked example: a 15 x 20 ft living room

Say the living room ceiling is 15 x 20 ft (4.6 x 6.1 m), unpainted popcorn, in a 1995 house with no asbestos concern after a clear test. The ceiling area is 15 x 20 = 300 sq ft.

- Scrape only at the low rate: 300 x $2 = $600.
- Scrape and skim coat at a typical $4 rate: 300 x $4 = $1,200.
- Full finish with primer and paint at the high rate: 300 x $6 = $1,800.

Check the math a second way. At $4 per square foot, a 100 sq ft patch of ceiling costs $400, and this room has three of those patches, so 3 x $400 = $1,200. The numbers match.

Budget $1,200 for the typical job and keep $1,800 in mind if you want it painted by the same crew. We rounded the budget up to the full-finish figure on purpose, because most owners do not stop at bare skim coat. Add a flat ceiling paint and a [primer calculator](/blog/primer-calculator/) check if you plan to finish it yourself after the crew leaves.

## Test for asbestos before you scrape

Popcorn texture sprayed on before the 1980s often contains asbestos. You cannot see it, smell it, or rule it out by the age of the house alone, because old stock was used into the early 1980s in some areas. The only safe answer is a lab test of a small sample, taken before any scraping, sanding, or drilling starts. The EPA explains the risks and when to call a trained professional in its homeowner guide, [Protect Your Family from Exposures to Asbestos](https://www.epa.gov/asbestos/protect-your-family-exposures-asbestos).

If the test comes back positive, stop. Do not scrape a positive ceiling yourself, do not sand it, and do not let a regular painter treat it like a normal job. Licensed abatement crews seal the room in plastic, keep the material wet, use filtered air machines, and bag the waste for approved disposal. That process is why asbestos work costs $5 to $20 per square foot instead of $1 to $6.

There are two safer options besides removal. A pro can cover the ceiling with new drywall, which seals the texture in place without disturbing it. You can also leave a sound, undamaged ceiling alone and paint it, since intact texture that nobody disturbs is far less of a risk than texture being scraped off. Water damage, crumbling edges, or a planned remodel change that call, so ask the testing firm what they advise for your ceiling, and check your state rules, because some states set their own notice and disposal rules for this work.

One more warning for older homes. Paint on the ceiling or trim from the same era can contain lead. If a quote includes sanding painted trim, ask how the crew handles lead-safe work.

## What pushes the price up or down?

Painted popcorn is the most common surprise. Texture that was never painted soaks up water, softens, and scrapes off in sheets. Paint seals the surface, so the crew has to work slower, score the paint, or sand, and the price moves toward the top of the range.

- Ceiling height over 9 ft (2.7 m) adds ladder and scaffold time to every step.
- Heavy texture and deep patches need a thicker skim coat, and some ceilings need two coats.
- Repairs under the texture, like water stains, cracked tape joints, and nail pops, get billed as extra patch work.
- Furniture in the room slows the crew down. An empty room with bare floors is the cheapest room to do.
- Disposal fees vary by town, and asbestos waste costs far more to haul than clean texture.

Whole-house jobs usually get a better rate per square foot than one small room. The crew sets up plastic and protection once, then moves room to room. If you plan to do several rooms this year, price them as one job and compare that total with the [cost to paint a house interior](/blog/cost-to-paint-house-interior/) if the same firm does both.

## Should you do it yourself or hire a pro?

DIY only makes sense after a clear asbestos test, on unpainted texture, in a room you can empty. Your costs are plastic sheeting, a garden sprayer, a wide scraper, joint compound, sanding supplies, primer, and paint, often $100 to $300 for one room. The real cost is your weekend. Scraping goes fast, but skim coating overhead is slow, tiring work, and every flaw shows once the light hits a smooth ceiling.

Hire a pro when the texture is painted, the ceiling is high, the area is large, or the skim coat has to be perfect in a bright room. Pros also handle the dust control and the bagging, which is the part most owners underestimate. Wet scraping still makes a heavy, soggy mess that has to leave the house in bags.

Never hire the cheapest bid without asking two questions. First, does the price include skim coating and sanding, or scraping only? Second, who handles testing, and what happens to the price if the test is positive? A fair quote answers both in writing. Compare the finished ceiling plan with our [how many coats of paint guide](/blog/how-many-coats-of-paint/) before you agree on who supplies the paint.

## Frequently asked questions

### How much does it cost to remove a popcorn ceiling in a 12 x 12 ft room?
The ceiling is 144 sq ft. At $1 to $6 per square foot, a pro charges about $145 to $865 depending on scope, with scrape and refinish near the middle of that range. Angi lists a standard 12 x 12 ft room at $145 to $430 for removal alone, before refinishing.

### Can I remove a popcorn ceiling myself?
Only after a lab test shows no asbestos, and only if the texture is unpainted and softens with water. If the test is positive, do not scrape it yourself at any price. Call a licensed abatement firm, or cover the ceiling with new drywall instead.

### How much does asbestos testing and removal add?
Testing is a small lab fee next to the job cost, but a positive result changes everything. Angi puts asbestos removal at $5 to $20 per square foot plus $75 to $200 per hour in specialist labor. A 300 sq ft ceiling can jump from about $1,200 to $1,500 to $6,000.

### How long does popcorn ceiling removal take?
Scraping one room takes a few hours, but skim coating, drying, sanding, and painting stretch most rooms over 2 to 3 days. Whole-house jobs run most of a week. Asbestos abatement adds days for containment, air checks, and approved disposal.

### Is it cheaper to cover a popcorn ceiling with drywall?
Sometimes. New drywall over the texture skips scraping and skim work, but you pay for sheets, hanging, taping, and finishing, plus you lose a little ceiling height. It is a smart option when the test is positive and abatement quotes come in high. Our [drywall calculator](/blog/drywall-calculator/) helps you count sheets for that route.

### Does removing a popcorn ceiling add home value?
It rarely adds a set dollar figure, but smooth ceilings make a dated home feel current, and buyers in older homes ask about asbestos. A clear test result and a clean, painted ceiling remove an objection. Keep the lab report with your house papers either way.

## Next step
Measure each ceiling, get the test done if your home predates the 1980s, then collect two quotes with the scope in writing. If fresh paint is part of the plan, run the room through our [cost to paint a room guide](/blog/cost-to-paint-a-room/) next so the ceiling and wall prices sit in one budget.

*Prices are US figures from 2026 and vary by region and supplier.*
